relevance_note: Case report of a family with GFAP-confirmed adult-onset Alexander disease: 'Whole exome sequencing found sibling 1 to be heterozygous for a missense substitution in GFAP p.N386S'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script in my scratch directory assembled the JSON and cut the Table 1 spans (patients as columns; column headers 'Neurologic findings - Sibling 1/2/3', labels 'Sibling 1/2/3' used as the paper's own labels). Script output was checked against Table 1 by eye. Table 1 symbols are garbled in the conversion ('11', '1', '2'); the legend in the table itself defines them ('11 5 Strongly present; 1 5 present; 2 5 absent'), so '2' cells are recorded as excluded with the legend quoted as a second span. Ages in Table 1 are in years per the row headings ('Age at ..., y'); 'Age at assessment, y' was used for age at last evaluation, although Siblings 1 and 2 had a reassessment 13 months later whose age is not given. Relatives in scope: the unaffected mother (tested by Sanger; her result is not stated explicitly, only that the mutation 'segregates with disease', so she has no variant row), the affected father (not tested; dementia, bulbar signs, spastic quadriplegia, died at 67) and the paternal aunt and grandfather (progressive parkinsonism; included as affected relatives, uncertain whether in scope). Variant printed as 'p.N386S (c.1157A.G; NM\_002055.4)': the cDNA string is recorded exactly as printed (the '>' is apparently lost in conversion) and the transcript value drops the Markdown escape backslash. Zygosity 'heterozygous' is stated only for sibling 1; siblings 2 and 3 are said to carry 'this mutation', so their zygosity is not reported. Inheritance not reported for all siblings (father untested; mother's negative result not stated explicitly). Sibling 1's sex is not stated. Sibling 1's text paragraph is split by page furniture (line ending 'compulsive' continues at 'behaviors. and insight emerged'); spans were not joined across the break, and 'no social or occupational impairment at initial assessment' was not recorded as an exclusion because the same sentence reports later functional deterioration. 'both'/'Both siblings' statements are attributed to Siblings 1 and 2 (the two who underwent neuropsychological testing, named in the preceding sentence). Contradiction: Sibling 2 'was diagnosed with depression' earlier, but 'Neither endorsed symptoms of depression or anxiety' on testing; both rows emitted (no checklist item affected). Tension (not a strict contradiction): Sibling 2 has Incontinence 'present' but Dysautonomia 'absent' in Table 1; the checklist item 'autonomic dysfunction (... bladder or bowel dysfunction ...)' was set observed from the Incontinence cell. Absent Hyperreflexia/Babinski and Nystagmus (Sibling 3) were not used to exclude the broader checklist items (pyramidal signs; eye movement abnormality). Bulbar signs were not mapped to dysphagia or dysarthria. Father's 'spastic quadriplegia' was taken as observed for both 'spasticity or pyramidal signs' and 'limb weakness'. MoCA scores and the Table 2 neuropsychological percentiles were not extracted as features; MRI findings are given only as 'MRI signs highly suggestive of AOAD' (figure e-1, not in the text), so all MRI checklist items are not reported. 'Structural imaging in this family did not indicate frontotemporal changes' was applied to the three siblings as a group statement. The Discussion's 'meeting criteria for possible bvFTD' for 'Their' profile was not recorded per person.
